statement: Make rs-raft the only partition consensus path. Today a production partition reaches the legacy backend by omission (RAFT_BACKEND_DEFAULT is liferaft and raftBackend is read only from PartitionService construction options that no production caller sets), and the partition write path is liferaft-shaped: applyWrite appends the entry to the legacy durable log through PartitionRaftStorage before proposing, so with rs-raft as the default the seed's first write during cache hydration dies (NOT NULL _raft_log.term) and 37 corpus files fail (census 2026-09-23). After this quest: normal PartitionService construction always yields the frozen rs-raft operation port with no selector, no default fallback and no raftProvider injection as an alternate semantic backend; a write is one propose() through the port whose committed-entry application applies it, with the rs-raft durable store as the only durable log (the legacy log adapter is never written on the partition write path, and the single-replica direct-execution bypass is gone because a solo rs-raft leader commits its own proposals); an explicit legacy backend name is a typed refusal; a partition database holding meaningful legacy consensus state and no rs-raft record fails closed with a typed outcome instead of being reused; and a restarted partition serves its writes from the rs-raft store. Proven by a seed node that bootstraps and serves CREATE TABLE, INSERT and SELECT through production construction with no backend selection at all.

constraints.statement: After this quest no production path constructs, selects, defaults to, or falls back to the legacy backend for a partition: not by omission, error, restart, snapshot recovery, worker path, or a test-shaped production option. The selector module and its default constant do not survive; a legacy backend name is refused by name.

A partition write is one propose() through the frozen operation port; application happens in the committed-entry callback the runtime owner already invokes. The rs-raft durable store is the only durable log; PartitionRaftStorage/SQLiteLogAdapter are never written on the write path, and the single-replica direct-execution branch is deleted rather than kept as a second path.

The frozen operation port keeps its twelve operations; no compatibility accessor, raw log, term or core reachability is added to satisfy the write path. The operation-boundary audit and its witnesses stay green.

A partition database with meaningful legacy consensus rows and no rs-raft record produces a typed startup outcome (legacy_partition_consensus_state_detected or the name the owner card fixes); there is no automatic log migration and no dual write. Mere existence of the historically named tables is not the detector.

Every witness expectation comes from production construction or the core (readStatus, the durable store on an independent connection, SELECT results), never from a test literal or the code path under test; each receipt must be red on the sealed head for the reason the census names.

Message groups, RaftGroup, RaftReplicaBase, WasmServiceReplica, snapshot catch-up ownership, pre_vote/check_quorum and runtime blast radius are recorded as findings for their own quests, never fixed here.

Source changes land only behind independent adversarial verification that attacks: an old-backend fallback, an alternate constructor, raw core reachability, stale durable-state reuse, a test stand-in instead of production engagement, and a second durable log.
